description: Add a contact create command that, inside the caller's transaction, checks contact:create for the actor, runs record-create authorization on the candidate's client (null included), performs the duplicate lookup, inserts through the contact model and queues the created event.

Project the duplicate-email outcome through the actor's read scope: an in-scope match may be named or returned; an out-of-scope or client-less match yields one generic in-use result with no client name and no contact.
Provide find-or-create as the same command returning the in-scope existing contact instead of failing, with scope checked before any lookup result is disclosed.
Route addContact, createClientContact and the contact CSV import create branch through the create command, so the scope check precedes the duplicate check on all three.
Route createOrFindContactByEmail through the command, keeping the client-portal own-client rule and removing the named-client error for callers who cannot read that client.
Route createOrFindIntegrationContactByEmail and createOrFindContact through the command so they require contact:create and client scope, and remove them from the pinned permission-coverage gaps.
Route REST contact create, ticket CSV import contact creation, and workflow contacts.create and contacts.duplicate with a user actor through the command.
Update the contact writer ledger contract so actor-initiated create paths must reach the command and only the named system writers insert directly.
Narrow findContactByEmailAddress, findIntegrationContactByEmailAddress and checkExistingEmails to the caller's contact read scope.
Grant create with the own_client condition on contact in the seat authority policy, and add contact:create to the Seat Technician role grants and the migration role catalog.
Add an additive, Citus-safe migration that gives contact:create to every existing Seat Technician role.
Show the contact picker's Add new affordance only to a user who may create a contact.
In the quick-add contact form, preselect, fix and require the client when the user's client scope resolves to exactly one client, and show the add-new-client affordance only with client:create.
Add the generic out-of-scope collision message to the locale files and surface it, and the in-scope existing-contact offer, in the quick-add contact form.
